To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the administration of corticosteroid during lactation is a valid tool to study the mother-offspring transfer of glucocorticoids and the role of maternal stress in the programming of individual phenotype; 2. the administration of exogenous corticosterone during the first days of life is a valid tool that allows the investigation of neonatal programming in the domains of emotional and immune regulation.
the administration of corticosteroids during lactation may program the offspring phenotype in a way that resembles the effect of environmental manipulations.
the administration of corticosteroids during the first week of lactation in rodents induces persistent changes in emotional and immune domains of the offspring's phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying the programming of individual phenotype in the context of maternal effects.
the investigation of the role of the neonatal maternal environment on individual phenotype and the development of novel paradigms for this purpose.
the study of individual phenotype and its modulation through environmental factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neonatal corticosterone exposure is a valid experimental tool to dissect the role of the maternal environment in the programming of the offspring's phenotype.
corticosterone administration during lactation can be used as a tool for the investigation of the maternal programming of individual phenotype.
the mother-offspring transfer paradigm represents a valuable tool to investigate the role of the neonatal maternal programming of the offspring's phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neonatal programming paradigm is a useful tool to dissect the role of maternal corticosterone transfer in the modulation of the offspring's phenotype and to identify the molecular mechanisms involved.
the neonatal programming can be considered a process of "maternal epigenetics" that is, a mechanism through which maternal experiences are translated to the developing individual's genome.
the neonatal administration of corticosteroid is a useful tool to dissect the mechanisms of maternal programming of individual phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neonatal programming is not a simple consequence of the short-term maternal responses to environmental challenges, but a complex process which is mediated by the mother's physiology, but also by the mother's behaviour and by the individual's own physiology.
the exogenous administration to lactating females of corticosterone can be used to study the neonatal programming effects of maternal stress in a more controlled and reproducible way.
neonatal corticosterone exposure can induce long-lasting modifications in emotional and immune domains in rodents.
